_comment: Canonical expected verdicts for the ARD reference lint. Any re-implementation of the lint must reproduce these. Runner: python3 run.py

version_anchor._comment: version-number anchor rule (CATALOGS §3 item 2), by fixture line. 'suppressed' lines must not fire version-number: the source-direct attestation tier, and cited lines whose resolved or reduced-substrate attestation contains the matched token. 'flagged' lines must fire: uncited; cited attestation lacks the token (incl. a prefix such as 3.1 vs 3.12, or a different 'version N'); a non-anchor citation status (intra-program, acquisition-candidate); one unanchored token among anchored ones. Dotted 'version N.M' is keyed on the whole dotted token: 'version 3.9' is not anchored by an attestation that only contains 'Version 3'. Token shapes: 'Version N' (any case) and standalone 'vN' are versions; tokens inside a citation, document locators (§3.4, Section 4.2, sections 1, 3.3-4.2), arXiv IDs and revisions, percentages and decimal statistics (kappa/Pearson/p = …, chained by 'vs') are not; numpy 1.26, R 4.3, 'or 3.12' and model names still fire. A bibliography entry line (N. **handle**, | N / handle |, ### N. Title — `handle`) is anchored by the attestation it names, under the same token rule; a candidate, missing handle or non-entry line still fires.

bare_citation._comment: Citation-form fence (CATALOGS §3 bare-citation): {N} with no [handle] is a broken chain at high severity; well-formed citations, ${N} / x_{N} / f{N}, inline code, URLs and fenced code do not fire.
